name: Latte
intro: A latte is a gentle, creamy drink of espresso mellowed by plenty of steamed milk and finished with a thin layer of foam. It's soft, slightly sweet from the milk, and easy to love. It's the cozy go-to for anyone who wants coffee without the sharp edge.
heroAlt: Engraved line illustration of a latte in a wide cup

vessel.name: Latte glass or large mug
vessel.note: The coaster recipe totals about 10 oz plus foam, so a 12 oz vessel gives breathing room.

ingredients.note: From roughly 18 g of finely ground coffee.
Whole milk gives the creamiest result.
Roughly a quarter inch (about 0.5 cm) on top.

equipment.alternative: Moka pot plus a handheld frother (see home methods)
Heat until the pitcher is hot to hold for only a few seconds

steps.title: Warm the glass
steps.body: Rinse your glass or mug with hot water. A latte is a bigger drink, and a cold vessel cools it down quickly.

steps.title: Pull the espresso
steps.body: Pull a double shot of espresso into your vessel. The milk will soften it, so a well-balanced shot, not a sour one, is the goal.
steps.tip: If lattes taste thin or milky, try a slightly finer grind for a stronger shot.

steps.title: Pour cold milk
steps.body: Fill a cold pitcher with about 8 oz of cold milk, plus a little extra to account for what clings to the pitcher. Cold milk gives you time to texture it before it overheats.

steps.title: Add a little air
steps.body: With the steam wand just under the surface, add air for only a couple of seconds. A latte wants a thin, smooth layer of foam, much less than a cappuccino.
steps.tip: You should hear a soft hiss, not loud slurping.

steps.title: Swirl and heat
steps.body: Lower the wand so the milk spins in a whirlpool until it reaches about 140°F. Spinning folds the air into the milk, making it glossy like wet paint, and temperature control keeps the milk sweet.
steps.tip: Swirl the pitcher and tap it to pop surface bubbles before pouring.

steps.title: Pour and finish
steps.body: Pour the milk into the espresso in a steady stream, finishing with a thin layer of foam on top. If you like latte art, bring the pitcher close and pour with a gentle wiggle.

homeMethods.note: Brew a moka pot and add warmed milk. It's cozy and rich, but the coffee is less concentrated than real espresso and has no crema.
Make a strong AeroPress shot and top with warm milk and handheld-frothed foam. It's a convincing homemade latte, though the texture is looser than steam-wand milk.
Strongly brewed coffee with warm frothed milk is closer to a café au lait than a latte. It's still tasty and comforting, but it won't have the espresso intensity.

tips: Milk should never boil, as overheated milk tastes flat and scalded.
Café sizes and espresso amounts vary, so this coaster recipe is a home-sized guideline.
commonMistakes: Adding too much air and making a foam-heavy drink.
Pouring too fast and breaking up the foam.
Using a weak shot that disappears under the milk.

variations.name: Flavored latte
variations.description: Add a pump or teaspoon of vanilla, caramel or other syrup to the cup before the espresso.

variations.name: Oat or almond latte
variations.description: Barista-style plant milks steam best, though results vary by brand.

variations.name: Iced latte
variations.description: See the Iced Latte page for the cold version.

history: In Italy, caffè latte simply means coffee with milk and has long been a home breakfast drink, and asking for a 'latte' alone there will get you plain milk. The popular café-style latte with espresso grew in popularity in the US and elsewhere in the late 20th century.

seo.title: How to Make a Latte at Home: Creamy Espresso and Steamed Milk
seo.description: Make a cozy latte with 2 oz espresso, 8 oz steamed milk and a thin layer of foam, with tips for milk texture and no-machine alternatives.
